8251.t: Uncertain. Commonly connected with Latin foedus (“ugly”).

8274.t: Beekes claims a Pre-Greek origin, due to the semantic category of lizards being "local substrate" and not being conceptualized among the Proto-Indo-Europeans.

8287.t: From earlier *σϝίγ- (*swíg-), probably of imitative origin.

8230.t: Perhaps from Ancient Greek πυραμός (pūramós) + -ίς (-ĭ́s), from πυρός (pūrós, “wheat”) + ἀμάω (amáō, “to reap”), or from Egyptian pr-m-ws (“height of a pyramid”), from pr (“(one that) comes forth”) + m (“from”) + ws (“height”).

8240.t: From the o-grade of πείρω (peírō, “to pierce, to run through”).

8255.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pótis, from Proto-Indo-European *pótis. Cognates include Albanian pata, Latin potis and Sanskrit पति॑ (páti).

8245.t: According to Beekes, from Proto-Indo-European *pélmn̥, from *pel- (“to cover, wrap; skin, hide; cloth”) and cognate with Proto-Germanic *felmô (“covering, skin”) (whence English film).

8258.t: Probably a substrate loanword from Italy, related to Latin buxus (“box tree”).

8221.t: From Proto-Indo-European *preh₃i, from *pró (“toward, leading to”). See also πρωΐ (prōĭ̈́, “morning”).

8244.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pélas, from Proto-Indo-European *pélh₂-s, from *pelh₂- (“to approach”).

8294.t: Probably of non-Indo-European (Pre-Greek substrate) origin, due to the alternating forms σιωπ- (sĭōp-) and σωπ- (sōp-).

8289.t: For plant names in -ύα (-ŭ́ā), compare οἰσύα (oisŭ́ā), ὀστρύα (ostrŭ́ā).

8213.t: Traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *pr̥so- (“leek”), and connected with Latin porrum (“leek”) and Albanian presh.

8253.t: From Proto-Hellenic *póiwā, from Proto-Indo-European *póyH-weh₂, from *peyH-. Cognate with Lithuanian pieva (“meadow”).

8239.t: From Proto-Indo-European *gʷʰedʰ- (“to request, pray, ask for”). Cognate with English bid (“to invite, command”), Sanskrit गाध (gādha, “desire, cupidity”).

8248.t: From Proto-Indo-European *pékʷonts (“cooking, ripening”); related to πέσσω (péssō, “to soften, ripen”).

8263.t: Late formation as the active equivalent of originally deponent σέβομαι (sébomai).

8252.t: Like many Greek words for pottery, most likely of Pre-Greek origin, as evidenced by the irregular variations between: * δ ~ θ (d ~ th), the former as in e.g. πίδος (pídos) * π ~ φ (p ~ ph), as in the derived terms πιθάκνη (pitháknē) ~ φιδάκνη (phidáknē)…

8280.t: From σείω (seíō, “I shake”) and the suffix -μα (-ma).

8222.t: According to Beekes, from a substrate root common to Proto-Slavic *brinъ (“larch”).

8295.t: According to Beekes, this word cannot be separated from σκιμβός (skimbós, “lame”) and the variation α ~ ι (a ~ i) as well as the derivatives with -υκ- (-uk-) and -αλ- (-al-) point to a Pre-Greek origin.

8279.t: Disputed. According to Beekes from Proto-Indo-European *kyew-, thus cognate with Sanskrit च्यु (cyu).

8281.t: Since Bezzenberger, traditionally compared with σάττω (sáttō, “to cram, to stuff”), though this suffers from phonetic issues. According to Beekes, the alternation rather points to Pre-Greek origin.

8220.t: In view of the close resemblance to Etruscan 𐌐𐌖𐌓𐌈𐌍𐌄 (purθne, “title of an official”), this word probably belongs to the Anatolian-Aegean stratum of social designations (compare ἄναξ (ánax), βασιλεύς (basileús) and τύραννος (túrannos)); attested with a…

8259.t: From πήγνυμι (pḗgnumi, “I stick, I fix”) + -σις (-sis, suffix to form a feminine noun).

8246.t: From Proto-Indo-European *(s)penh₁- (“to weave, spin”), with semantic shift "to weave, stretch" > "to tense, strain" > "to exert oneself".

8261.t: The existence and meaning of this word is disputed. It was interpreted by some early scholars as a phonetic rendering of an Old Persian word, possibly *xšaθram (“realm, kingdom”).
